description: RISK R-B, STATED FIRST BECAUSE THE CLASS NAME INVERTS THE BEHAVIOUR: the prompt-mandated Java class for COTRN02C is TransactionViewController, and this program does not view - it ADDS. Two independent artefacts say so and they agree with each other rather than with the name: app/cbl/COTRN02C.cbl:5 reads 'Function    : Add a new Transaction to TRANSACT file', and README.md:222 records 'CT02 | COTRN02 | COTRN02C | Transaction Add' directly beneath README.md:221's 'CT01 | COTRN01 | COTRN01C | Transaction View' - the inverse of the prompt's mapping, whose other half is parity/COTRN01C where the source genuinely views. Rule R1 resolves it: the name comes from the prompt and the behaviour comes from the source, so nothing here is renamed and no case in this folder is downgraded to a read-only expectation. Per practice B4 the conflict is documented rather than corrected - the Agent Action Plan escalates it for explicit user confirmation, and this case states it rather than quietly reconciling it. PROVENANCE, RISK R-A AND PRACTICE B12: every expected value below was derived by reading app/cbl/COTRN02C.cbl against the copybook layouts - the xxxI widths of app/cpy-bms/COTRN02.CPY, the 160-byte CARDDEMO-COMMAREA of app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy plus the 58-byte CDEMO-CT02-INFO the program appends at :72-80 for a passed area of 218, the two PIC X(40) title literals of app/cpy/COTTL01Y.cpy, the 50-byte CARD-XREF-RECORD of app/cpy/CVACT03Y.cpy - and the real app/data/ASCII fixtures. It was NOT captured from a live COBOL run: executing the legacy programs is impossible in this environment, and the Agent Action Plan records eight independently verified blockers for it, including a COBOL compiler whose indexed-file handler is disabled, no Language Environment CEE* service behind CSUTLDTC, no CICS emulator, and the absence of the IBM-supplied DFHAID and DFHBMSCA copybooks this program copies at :92-93 (risk R-D, which is why the AID is named by mnemonic through common.CicsAid and the colour through common.BmsAttributes). A statically derived expectation can encode a misreading where a captured one cannot, so every claim here names the line it came from. WHAT THIS CASE DRIVES: arm three of VALIDATE-INPUT-KEY-FIELDS at :193-230, which is an EVALUATE TRUE of three arms whose first match wins and whose WHEN OTHER is last (gate G30). In source order they are: arm one at :196, ACTIDINI NOT = SPACES AND LOW-VALUES, which numeric-tests the account id at :197, converts it with FUNCTION NUMVAL at :204, reads the CXACAIX alternate-index path at :208 and writes the card number back onto the screen at :209 - exercised by cases 07, 08, 09 and 10; arm two at :210, the same shape for CARDNINI, reading the CCXREF base cluster at :222 and writing the account id back at :223 - exercised by cases 11, 12, 13 and 14; and arm three at :224-229, WHEN OTHER, which is THIS case. Both guards are the abbreviated combined relation NOT = SPACES AND LOW-VALUES, so a field holding spaces satisfies neither: ACTIDINI arrives as eleven spaces and CARDNINI as sixteen, the EVALUATE falls through to its default, and :225-227 raise WS-ERR-FLG and move the literal 'Account or Card Number must be entered...' - with its three trailing dots, which are part of the literal and are not an abbreviation of anything - into WS-MESSAGE. Because arm one is tested before arm two, a screen carrying BOTH keys resolves through the account and has its card number overwritten from the cross-reference; this case is the complement of that asymmetry, where neither key was supplied at all. THE SHORT-CIRCUIT, WHICH IS THE ONLY CONTROL-FLOW SUBTLETY IN THIS PROGRAM: :228 moves -1 into ACTIDINL and :229 performs SEND-TRNADD-SCREEN, and that paragraph ends at :530-534 with EXEC CICS RETURN TRANSID('CT02') COMMAREA(CARDDEMO-COMMAREA). In CICS a RETURN terminates the task, so control never comes back to PROCESS-ENTER-KEY: the PERFORM VALIDATE-INPUT-DATA-FIELDS at :167 never runs and the EVALUATE CONFIRMI at :169 is never reached. Four consequences are asserted here rather than assumed. expectedMessages carries exactly ONE message text - the key-field literal - recorded on the two channels whose widths the copybooks fix: WS-MESSAGE is PIC X(80) and ERRMSGO is PIC X(78), so MOVE WS-MESSAGE TO ERRMSGO at :520 space-pads the 41-character literal on the right at each width and would discard the last two bytes of a longer one (rule R5); there is no 'can NOT be empty' message from the eleven-arm cascade at :251-320 and no 'Confirm to add this transaction...' prompt from :178. expectedWrites is EMPTY and TRANSACT still holds exactly its three seeded rows, which is the load-bearing assertion of this case: the screen arrives with all eleven detail fields well formed - type 01, category 0001, a POS TERM source, an amount of +00000012.34 in the positional -99999999.99 shape the check at :339-351 demands, two 2022-07-18 dates that both pass :353-381 and that CSUTLDTC accepts with severity '0000', and a nine-digit merchant id - AND with CONFIRMI holding 'Y', so had the task continued, :170 would have taken the first arm of the EVALUATE CONFIRMI and ADD-TRANSACTION would have written a 350-byte record at :713. Nothing is written, because the guard fires first and the detail fields are never examined. expectedReturnCode is 0: COTRN02C is an online program, it sets no RETURN-CODE and contains zero CALL 'CEE3ABD' occurrences, so no abend path exists anywhere in this folder. And there is NO dataset I/O at all - neither the CXACAIX path at :578 nor the CCXREF base at :611 is read, because neither key arm matched - so the cross-reference is seeded and deliberately left untouched, which is a stronger statement than not seeding it. WHAT IS AND IS NOT HIGHLIGHTED (gate G38, REENTER half): the request arrives with CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT = 1, so :120 takes the else branch, :132 receives the map and the EVALUATE EIBAID at :133 takes its DFHENTER arm at :134. This is therefore the re-entered state in which an error highlight would apply - and this screen highlights in NEITHER state, which is how it satisfies the gate. COTRN02C does not copy CSSETATY (its copybook list at :71-93 does not name it) and declares no per-field FLG-NOT-OK switch, so no rejecting arm moves an attribute byte: ERRMSGC carries the map's default colour DFHDFCOL rather than DFHRED, no field is starred, and the program's only attribute assignment anywhere is MOVE DFHGREEN TO ERRMSGC at :727 on the successful-write path, which this case does not reach. The one piece of field metadata this arm does set is the cursor: MOVE -1 TO ACTIDINL at :228, recorded as cursorField because COBOL positions the cursor by moving -1 into a field's xxxL item. ACTIDINL is a length item, and xxxL, xxxF and xxxA items are validation and highlight metadata rather than payload, so it appears as metadata and never as a screen field; -1 reaches ACTIDINL and no other length item. Conversation state travels entirely in the payload - the 218-byte area, the AID and the map values - and no session is kept (rule R6, gate G37); the task ends at the RETURN rather than an XCTL, so there is no nextProgram transfer on this path and the response simply names this program, its own mapset COTRN02 and its own map COTRN2A for the next call. ACCTDAT IS A DEAD DECLARATION AND STAYS ONE (practice B5): :40 declares WS-ACCTDAT-FILE PIC X(08) VALUE 'ACCTDAT ' and :89 copies CVACT01Y, and no EXEC CICS command in the program names either - so the account file appears in no expectedRecords entry in any case in this folder, and it is not seeded here either, because the unit is constructed with no AccountRepository at all and no observed channel could report one. Only the two datasets the source actually reaches are seeded, by BINDING KEY and never by a dataset name (gate G46): TRANSACT with three 350-byte rows declared inline, and the cross-reference as ONE dataset under the CCXREF base key, seeded from the real fixtures/cardxref.txt. CXACAIX is not seeded separately - app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD defines it as an ALTERNATE INDEX TO CCXREF VIA ACCOUNT KEY over the same base cluster, so it is a finder on one repository and never a second table (gate G45). The fixture rows are declared RAW at 36 bytes and are not pre-padded: CVACT03Y declares 50 - XREF-CARD-NUM X(16), XREF-CUST-ID 9(09), XREF-ACCT-ID 9(11) and FILLER X(14) - and the data omits the trailing FILLER, so the 36-to-50 pad is declared as a normalisation and performed by parity/FieldDiffer, which is its sole owner (gate G16, risk R-F). The clock is pinned to the same instant every case in this folder pins, 2022-07-19T23:12:34, so the two header items POPULATE-HEADER-INFO builds from FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE at :554 - the date as mm/dd/yy from a year taken as WS-CURDATE-YEAR(3:2) at :563, and the time as hh:mm:ss - are comparable byte for byte (practice B7), and the code page is named US-ASCII rather than left to the platform default (practice B8). GOVERNING RULES: review_rules returns exactly one line, 'No user rules provided', which is the whole document - so no user rule governs this file, and that absence is stated rather than treated as licence to lower the bar. The standard held instead is the Agent Action Plan's enterprise practices, cited where they bite: B1 (no placeholder - the message is the source literal), B3 (every reference tree read-only), B4, B5, B7, B8, B11 (every width taken from a PICTURE clause) and B12, together with rules R1, R5, R6 and R7 - and R7 costs nothing extra here, since COTRN02C contains zero GO TO statements and the arm order above is the whole of its control flow. The unit is reached as a plain controller object with no HTTP layer, no MockMvc and no JobLauncher in the path (gate G51), and this case is complete only when its diff count is zero (gate G18) - as one of the twenty cases the program's gate requires and parity/ParityHarness enforces by name, case01 through case20 with no gap and no duplicate (gate G15).
